title: Account triage sprintboard for quarterly engagements
summary: Working sprintboard to help CS managers and AEs triage accounts for the upcoming quarterly business reviews and renewal outreach. This doc converts a lightweight segmentation matrix into a prioritized sprint (two-week cadence) with explicit owners, outreach templates, and escalation paths. Purpose: focus limited field resources on accounts with the highest renewal impact and technical risk across deployment modes and regions.
scoring_rubric: Priority score = 100 weighted. Weights: ARR share (40%), ICP fit (15%), Deployment sensitivity (private/VPC/on-prem) (15%), Health score (10%), Usage trend last 30d (10%), Upcoming renewal within 90d (10%). Example: ARR contribution normalized to percentile -> *40. ICP fit: 0 (low) / 7.5 (mid) / 15 (high). Deployment sensitivity: 0 (hosted) / 7.5 (dedicated) / 15 (private). Health score: 0-10 scaled to 0-10. Usage trend: -10..+10 mapped to 0..10. Renewal urgency: within 90d=10, 91-180d=5, >180d=0.

action_playbook: High priority (score >=80): Immediate cross-functional sync (CSM + AE + Solutions + SRE). Host executive QBR within 7 business days. Offer targeted concessions: limited free dedicated hours, technical concierge, or contract flex to prevent churn.

Medium priority (60-79): Schedule technical deep-dive + adoption workshop. Prepare cost/latency optimizations (batching, quantization suggestions). Use canary billing/legal play templates for negotiation.
Monitor (40-59): 30-day check-in cadence with usage nudges, targeted enablement (help center articles, 1:1 office hours). Track signal changes weekly; escalate if health or ARR trend worsens.
Low-touch (<40): Automated lifecycle emails, renewal reminders 60/30/14 days out, standard contract renewals with self-serve options. No field time unless signal changes occur.
region_notes: EMEA: Privacy and compliance items carry extra weight — ICP fit bumped +5 points for regulated sectors. Always attach compliance artifact checklist for private deployments.
NA: Price sensitivity high for mid-market; focus messaging on unit economics and cost-savings from batching/caching.
APAC/LATAM: Ensure local support hours aligned; prioritize timezone-matched CS owners for high-priority accounts.
deployment_mode_risks: Hosted: lowest technical lock-in but higher price sensitivity; fallback options easier. Escalate for churn risk mostly on product adoption signals.
Dedicated: moderate risk — predictable throughput but capacity/overprovision concerns. Proactive capacity planning and autoscale options should be offered.
Private (VPC/on-prem/air-gapped): highest operational risk — involve SRE + security early. Renewals often tied to compliance audits; timeline friction common.
escalation_paths: Tier A+: CSM -> Senior CSM -> Solutions Eng -> Head of Customer Success. Exec sponsor loop if renewal at-risk.
Tier A/B: CSM -> Solutions Eng -> AE for commercial concessions.
Tier C/D: CSM -> AE only if commercial negotiation required.
review_checklist: Confirm ARR and contract term in SFDC (owner: AE)
Verify last 90d usage graph and health anomalies (owner: CSM)
Check deployment mode and open infra tickets (owner: Solutions Eng)
Attach compliance artifacts if private deployment (owner: Security/CSM)
Prepare recommended optimizations (batches/kv caching/quantization) with estimated cost delta (owner: Product Ops)
Lock calendar for QBR outreach and exec invites (owner: AE/CSM)
Update sprintboard status: todo / in-progress / blocked / done (owner: CSM)
Add outcome and renewal decision note post-QBR (owner: CSM)
If at-risk, create JIRA ticket and tag retention path (owner: CSM)
If healthy and expansion candidate, create upsell motion with AE and set follow-up in 30 days (owner: AE)
Record any legal/discount approvals in linked_artifacts
notes: This is a working draft for the upcoming QBR cycle — intended to be edited collaboratively. Use the sample_rows as a seed for exporting into a sheet when converting to a sprint tracker. Key open questions: how to weight strategic reference accounts vs pure ARR; whether to include NPS as independent weight for 2026 Q2; and whether to auto-promote accounts to A tier if they have air-gapped private deployments plus >$500k ARR. Please comment inline and flag accounts for which data is missing (renewal date, ARR, or health).
